While gasoline is mainly a consumer fuel for cars, diesel powers much of the wider economy, from freight transport and farming equipment to construction and industry. That is why diesel shortages or price shocks can have a bigger economic impact than higher gasoline prices by raising the cost of moving goods and operating heavy machinery. As businesses become strained, these higher energy costs will be passed on to consumers and add to a growing cost-of-living crisis and inflation . So what's driving global diesel prices higher?
